methodology: Curated seed dataset. Records are summaries of primary publisher sources. Legal force is classified by instrument type; this is not a jurisdiction-wide strictness ranking. Relevance to agentic AI is assessed separately from legal status.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence Act — Regulation (EU) 2024/1689
records.summary: Horizontal, risk-based AI legislation establishing obligations for providers, deployers and other actors. Its relevance to financial institutions depends on the AI system's intended purpose, role and classification; not every financial AI use is automatically high-risk.
records.agent_notes: Agentic systems are not a standalone legal category in the Act. Assess the system's functions, autonomy, intended purpose, provider/deployer role and any applicable high-risk classification. GPAI, transparency, prohibited-practice and governance provisions may also be relevant.
records.current_timeline: Entered into force 1 Aug 2024. Prohibitions and AI literacy obligations applied from 2 Feb 2025; GPAI obligations and governance provisions from 2 Aug 2025. Following the 2026 AI Omnibus, Annex III high-risk rules are scheduled for 2 Dec 2027 and Annex I product-related high-risk rules for 2 Aug 2028. Verify transitional details against the current official timeline.
records.verification_note: Official European Commission policy page and EUR-Lex legislation checked. Application dates reflect the Commission's current implementation timeline at verification date.
records.caveat: This record is an analytical summary, not legal advice. Classification is use-case-specific.

records.title: Digital Operational Resilience Act — Regulation (EU) 2022/2554
records.issuer: European Parliament and Council; supervised by European Supervisory Authorities and competent authorities
records.agent_relevance: Indirect but material to AI-enabled ICT
records.summary: Establishes harmonised digital operational resilience requirements for financial entities, including ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and ICT third-party risk oversight.
records.agent_notes: DORA is not an AI-agent regulation. It can nevertheless apply where AI agents, models, cloud platforms, APIs or other agent dependencies form part of a financial entity's ICT systems or third-party service arrangements.
records.verification_note: EUR-Lex official regulation and application date checked.
records.caveat: AI-agent relevance is an application analysis, not an express AI-agent-specific provision.

records.title: AI in financial services: good practice and areas for improvement
records.short_title: FCA AI good and poor practice
records.summary: FCA publication drawing on supervisory work and industry engagement. It explains how existing UK regulatory requirements apply to firms' AI use and describes good and poor practice in governance, accountability, human oversight, monitoring and consumer outcomes.
records.agent_notes: The FCA states that existing rules apply to firms' AI use. For agentic deployments, firms should map autonomy, delegated actions, escalation, monitoring, audit trails and accountability to the applicable existing requirements.
records.current_timeline: Published 19 Oct 2026; page last updated 20 Oct 2026.
records.verification_note: FCA publication page and publication/update dates checked.
records.caveat: The publication itself is not a new standalone binding AI regulation; it explains expectations under existing rules.

records.title: Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management for Financial Institutions
records.summary: MAS guidelines set out supervisory expectations for financial institutions managing risks arising from AI use. They apply across AI technologies and call for proportionate lifecycle controls, inventories, materiality assessment, governance, testing, human oversight, cybersecurity and third-party risk management.
records.agent_notes: MAS expressly anticipates greater use of agentic AI systems that operate autonomously and access tools, and states that it intends to consult further on additional agentic-AI guidance in 2027.
records.current_timeline: Published 7 Oct 2026; guidelines take effect 7 Oct 2027. MAS indicated further consultation on agentic-AI guidance in 2027.
records.verification_note: MAS official guidelines page and stated effective date checked.
records.caveat: Do not describe the guidelines as already effective before 7 Oct 2027.

records.title: Safeguards for Agentic Finance at Runtime (SAFR)
records.issuer: Industry participants under MAS BuildFin.ai initiative
records.summary: Industry-developed framework proposing runtime safeguards for AI agents performing financial tasks, including authorisation of agent actions, activation of human oversight and recording at decision points.
records.agent_notes: Highly relevant technical and governance reference for agentic financial workflows. It is not legislation or a binding MAS rule; record it as an industry framework associated with a regulator-supported initiative.
records.verification_note: MAS publication record checked; framework described as jointly developed by industry under BuildFin.ai.
records.caveat: Regulator-hosted publication does not make the industry framework legally binding.

records.title: Sound Practices for Responsible Adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI): Final Report
records.summary: FSB report sets out 12 sound practices for financial institutions, covering organisation-wide governance and AI lifecycle risk management from development through deployment. Topics include materiality, data governance, explainability, performance, human oversight, cyber and ICT risk, and third-party dependencies.
records.agent_notes: The report expressly recognises rapid advances in generative and agentic AI. It is a high-value global supervisory reference, but it does not itself create directly enforceable obligations in national law.
records.current_timeline: Final report published 15 Oct 2026 following June 2026 consultation.
records.verification_note: FSB official final report page checked.
records.caveat: Non-binding. National implementation and supervisory uptake vary by jurisdiction.

records.title: Financial Services AI Risk Management Framework (FS AI RMF)
records.agent_relevance: General AI relevance; agent application by analogy
records.summary: Treasury released a financial-services-specific AI Risk Management Framework and a shared AI lexicon to support a common understanding and practical risk management for AI use in the financial sector.
records.agent_notes: Use as a financial-sector risk-management reference. Agent-specific controls should be mapped explicitly rather than assumed to be addressed in detail by the framework.
records.caveat: Framework is a resource, not a generally binding regulation.

records.title: AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0)
records.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
records.agent_relevance: General AI relevance; agent application by analogy
financial_scope: Cross-sector; applicable as a reference to financial services
records.summary: NIST voluntary framework helps organisations incorporate trustworthiness considerations into the design, development, use and evaluation of AI systems. NIST indicates that AI RMF 1.0 is being revised.
records.agent_notes: Useful for structuring risk identification, measurement, management and governance. It is not specifically an AI-agent or financial-sector regulation; pair with agent-specific security frameworks and financial-sector rules.
records.current_timeline: Released 26 Jan 2023; revision underway as of the official NIST page checked 7 Nov 2026.
records.verification_note: NIST official AI RMF page checked; voluntary status and revision note confirmed.
records.caveat: Voluntary framework; legal effect depends on adoption or incorporation into other requirements.

records.title: AI Agent Standards Initiative for Interoperable and Secure Innovation
records.issuer: NIST Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI)
financial_scope: Cross-sector; relevant to financial institutions using agents
records.summary: NIST initiative aims to support secure, interoperable AI agents and development of standards and protocols for agents capable of autonomous actions.
records.agent_notes: Directly agent-specific and relevant to identity, interoperability, secure delegation and agent-to-agent interactions. The announcement is an initiative, not itself a completed technical standard or regulation.
records.caveat: Do not classify this initiative as an adopted standard or binding requirement.

records.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications
financial_scope: Cross-sector; relevant to financial agent deployments
records.summary: Security-focused taxonomy and guidance addressing risks in agentic applications. It provides a technical vocabulary for analysing agent-specific attack surfaces and mitigations.
records.agent_notes: Use as a technical threat reference, not as legislation or a financial-sector supervisory standard. Map each risk to financial consequences and applicable controls separately.
records.current_timeline: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026 resource published 9 Dec 2025.
records.verification_note: OWASP official resource page and 9 Dec 2025 publication date checked.
records.caveat: Technical guidance, not regulation. Treat as a community-developed security framework.

records.title: In data we trust? Emerging policy and supervisory approaches to AI data use in financial services
records.issuer: Bank for International Settlements — Financial Stability Institute
records.agent_relevance: General AI relevance; agent application by analogy
records.summary: BIS FSI paper examines data-related challenges in financial-sector AI, including privacy, quality, security, third-party dependencies and concentration among service providers, and analyses supervisory approaches.
records.agent_notes: Important for agent memory, context, retrieval, tool inputs and third-party data dependencies. It is research, not a binding supervisory instrument.
records.caveat: Research publication; does not create legal obligations.

records.title: AI Adoption Plan: Financial Services
records.short_title: UK Financial Services AI Adoption Plan
records.summary: Independent AI Champions' adoption plan recommends actions for government, regulators and industry to accelerate safe AI adoption in UK financial services. Its recommendations cover regulatory framework, resilience and agentic payments among other areas.
records.agent_notes: Agentic payments are explicitly included among the areas addressed. Track follow-on government and regulator actions separately; the report itself is not binding legislation.
records.caveat: Recommendations and policy plan, not a binding instrument.
